19.9: Then all the people were at strife thorowout all the tribes of Israel, saying, The King saved us out of the hand of our enemies, and he delivered us out of the hand of the Philistims, and now he is fled out of the land for Absalom.
19.10: And Absalom, whom we anoynted over us, is dead in battel: therefore why are ye so slow to bring the King again?
19.11: But King David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the Priestes, saying, Speak unto the Elders of Judah, and say, Why are ye behind to bring the King again to his house, (for the saying of al Israel is come unto the king, even to his house)
19.12: Ye are my brethren: my bones and my flesh are ye: wherefore then are ye the last that bring the King again?
19.13: Also say ye to Amasa, Art thou not my bone and my flesh? God do so to me and more also, if thou be not captain of the host to me for ever in the roume of Joab.
19.14: So he bowed the heartes of all the men of Judah, as of one man: therefore they sent to the King, saying, Return thou with all thy servants.
19.15: So the King returned, and came to Iorden. And Judah came to Gilgal, for to goe to meet the King, and to conduct him over Iorde.
19.16: And Shimei the sonne of Gera, ye sonne of Iemini, which was of Bahurim, hasted and came down with the men of Judah to meet king David,
19.17: And a thousand men of Beniamin with him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sonnes and twentie servants with him: and they went over Iorden before ye king.
19.18: And there went over a boat to carie over the Kings houshold, and to do him pleasure. Then Shimei the sonne of Gera fell before the King, when he was come over Iorden,
19.19: And said unto the King, Let not my lord impute wickedness unto me, nor remember ye thing that thy servant did wickedly when my lord the King departed out of Jerusalem, that the King should take it to his heart.
19.20: For thy servant doeth know, that I have done amiss: therefore behold, I am the first this day of al the house of Joseph, that am come to goe down to meet my lord the King.
19.21: But Abishai the sonne of Zeruiah answered, and said, Shal not Shimei die for this, because he cursed the Lordes anoynted?
19.22: And David said, What have I to do with you, ye sonnes of Zeruiah, that this day ye should be adversaries unto me? shall there any man die this day in Israel? for doe not I know that I am this day King over Israel?
19.23: Therefore the King said unto Shimei, Thou shalt not die, and the king sware unto him.
19.24: And Mephibosheth the sonne of Saul came down to meet the king, and had neither washed his feet, nor dressed his beard, nor washed his clothes from the time the king departed, until he returned in peace.
19.25: And when he was come to Jerusalem, and met the king, the king said unto him, Wherefore wentest not thou with me, Mephibosheth?
19.26: And he answered, My lord the king, my servant deceived me: for thy servant said, I would have mine ass sadled to ride thereon, for to goe with the king, because thy servant is lame.
19.27: And he hath accused thy servant unto my lord the king: but my lord the king is as an Angel of God: doe therefore thy pleasure.
19.28: For all my fathers house were but dead men before my lord the king, yet diddest thou set thy servant among them that did eat at thine own table: what right therefore have I yet to cry any more unto the king?
19.29: And the king said unto him, Why speakest thou any more of thy matters? I have said, Thou, and Ziba deuide the landes.
19.30: And Mephibosheth said unto the king, Yea, let him take all, seeing my lord the king is come home in peace.
19.31: Then Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim, and went over Iorden with the king, to conduct him over Iorden.
19.32: Now Barzillai was a very aged man, even fourescore yeere old, and he had provided the king of sustenance, while he lay at Mahanaim: for he was a man of very great substance.
19.33: And the king said unto Barzillai, Come over with me, and I will feed thee with me in Jerusalem.
19.34: And Barzillai said unto the king, How long have I to live, that I should goe up with the king to Jerusalem?
19.35: I am this day fourescore yeere old: and can I discern between good or evil? Hath thy servant any taste in that I eat or in that I drink? Can I hear any more the voyce of singing men and women? wherefore then should thy servant be anymore a burthen unto my lord the king?
19.36: Thy servant will goe a litle way over Iorden with the King, and why wil the king recompence it me with such a reward?
19.37: I pray thee, let thy servant turn back again, that I may die in mine own citie, and be buryed in the grave of my father and of my mother: but behold thy servant Chimham, let him goe with my lord the king, and doe to him what shall please thee.
19.38: And the king answered, Chimham shall go with me, and I will do to him that thou shalt be content with: and whatsoever thou shalt require of me, that will I do for thee.
19.39: So all the people went over Iorden: and the King passed over: and the King kissed Barzillai, and blessed him, and hee returned unto his own place.
19.40: Then the King went to Gilgal, and Chimham went with him, and all the people of Judah conducted the King, and also half ye people of Israel.
19.41: And behold, all the men of Israel came to the King, and sayd unto the King, Why have our brethren the men of Judah stolen thee away, and have brought the King and his houshold, and all Dauids men with him over Iorden?
19.42: And all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, Because the King is neere of kin to us: and wherefore now be ye angry for this matter? have we eaten of the Kings cost, or have wee taken any bribes?
19.43: And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, and said, Wee have ten partes in the King, and have also more right to David then ye: Why then did ye despise us, that our advise should not bee first had in restoring our King? And the wordes of the men of Judah were fiercer then the wordes of the men of Israel.

20.1: Then there was come thither a wicked man (named Sheba the sonne of Bichri, a man of Iemini) and hee blew the trumpet, and said, Wee have no part in David, neither have we inheritance in the sonne of Ishai: every man to his tents, O Israel.
20.2: So every man of Israel went from David and followed Sheba the sonne of Bichri: but the men of Judah clave fast unto their King, from Iorden even to Jerusalem.
20.3: When David then came to his house to Jerusalem, the King took the ten women his concubines, that hee had left behind him to keep the house, and put them in ward, and fed them, but lay no more with them: but they were enclosed unto the day of their death, living in widowhode.
20.4: Then sayde the King to Amasa, Assemble me the men of Judah within three dayes, and be thou here present.
20.5: So Amasa went to assemble Judah, but hee taried longer then the time which he had appoynted him.
20.6: Then David sayd to Abishai, Now shall Sheba the sonne of Bichri doe us more harm then did Absalom: take thou therefore thy lords servants and follow after him, lest he get him walled cities, and escape us.
20.7: And there went out after him Ioabs men, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and all the mightie men: and they departed out of Jerusalem, to follow after Sheba the sonne of Bichri.
20.8: When they were at the great stone, which is in Gibeon, Amasa went before them, and Ioabs garment, that hee had put on, was girded unto him, and upon it was a sword girded, which hanged on his loynes in the sheath, and as hee went, it used to fall out.
20.9: And Joab sayde to Amasa, Art thou in health, my brother? and Joab took Amasa by the beard with the right hand to kiss him.
20.10: But Amasa took no heed to the sword that was in Ioabs hand: for therewith he smote him in the fift rib, and shed out his bowels to the ground, and smote him not the second time: so he dyed. then Joab and Abishai his brother followed after Sheba the sonne of Bichri.
20.11: And one of Ioabs men stood by him, and said, He that fauoureth Joab, and hee that is of Dauids part, let him go after Joab.
20.12: And Amasa wallowed in blood in the mids of the way: and when the man saw that all the people stood still, he remooued Amasa out of the way into the field, and cast a cloth upon him, because he saw that every one that came by him, stood still.
20.13: When hee was removed out of the way, euerie man went after Joab, to follow after Sheba the sonne of Bichri.
20.14: And he went through all the tribes of Israel unto Abel, and Bethmaachah and all places of Berim: and they gathered together, and went also after him.
20.15: So they came, and besieged him in Abel, neere to Bethmaachah: and they cast up a mount against the citie, and the people thereof stood on the ramper, and al the people that was with Joab, destroyed and cast down the wall.
20.16: Then cried a wise woman out of the citie, Hear, hear, I pray you, say unto Joab, Come thou hither, that I may speak with thee.
20.17: And when hee came neere unto her, the woman said, Art thou Joab? And he answered, Yea. And she said to him, Hear the wordes of thine handmaid. And he answered, I do hear.
20.18: Then she spake thus, They spake in the old time, saying, They should ask of Abel. and so have they continued.
20.19: I am one of them, that are peaceable and faithful in Israel: and thou goest about to destroy a citie, and a mother in Israel: why wilt thou deuoure the inheritance of the Lord?
20.20: And Joab answered, and said, God forbid, God forbid it me, that I should deuoure, or destroy it.
20.21: The matter is not so, but a man of mout Ephraim (Sheba ye sonne of Bichri by name) hath lift up his had against ye King, even against David: deliver us him onely, and I will depart from the citie. And the woman said unto Joab, Behold, his head shalbe throwen to thee over the wall.
20.22: Then the woman went unto all the people with her wisedome, and they cut off the head of Sheba the sonne of Bichri, and cast it to Joab: the he blew the trumpet, and they retired from the citie, every man to his tent: and Joab returned to Jerusalem unto the King.
20.23: Then Joab was over all the host of Israel, and Benaiah the sonne of Jehoiada over the Cherethites and over the Pelethies,
20.24: And Adoram over the tribute, and Joshaphat the sonne of Ahilud the recorder,
20.25: And Sheia was Scribe, and Zadok and Abiathar the Priests,
20.26: And also Ira the Jairite was chief about David.

21.1: Then there was a famine in the dayes of David, three yeeres together: and David asked counsel of the Lord, and the Lord answered, It is for Saul, and for his bloodie house, because hee slew the Gibeonites.
21.2: Then ye King called the Gibeonites and said unto them. (Now the Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel, but a remnant of the Amorites, unto whom ye children of Israel had sworn: but Saul sought to slay them for his zeal toward the children of Israel and Judah)
21.3: And David said unto the Gibeonites, What shall I doe for you, and wherewith shall I make the atonement, that ye may bless the inheritance of the Lord?
21.4: The Gibeonites then answered him, Wee will have no silver nor gold of Saul nor of his house, neither for us shalt thou kill any man in Israel. And he said, What ye shall say, that will I doe for you.
21.5: Then they answered the King, The man that consumed us and that imagined evil against us, so that we are destroyed from remaining in any coast of Israel,
21.6: Let seven men of his sonnes be delivered unto us, and we will hang them up unto the Lord in Gibeah of Saul, the Lordes chosen. And the King said, I will give them.
21.7: But the King had compassion on Mephibosheth the sonne of Jonathan the sonne of Saul, because of the Lordes othe, that was between them, even between David and Jonathan the sonne of Saul.
21.8: But the King took the two sonnes of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bare unto Saul, even Armoni and Mephibosheth and the five sonnes of Michal, the daughter of Saul, whom she bare to Adriel the sonne of Barzillai the Meholathite.
21.9: And hee delivered them unto the handes of the Gibeonites, which hanged them in the mountain before the Lord: so they died all seven together, and they were slain in the time of harvest: in the first dayes, and in the beginning of barly harvest.
21.10: Then Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackecloth and hanged it up for her upon the rock, from the beginning of harvest, until water dropped upon them from the heaven, and suffered neither the birdes of the air to light on the by day, nor beasts of the field by night.
21.11: And it was told David, what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah ye concubine of Saul had done.
21.12: And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his sonne from the citizens of Jabesh Gilead, which had stolen them from the street of Beth-shan, where the Philistims had hanged them, when the Philistims had slain Saul in Gilboa.
21.13: So hee brought thence the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his sonne, and they gathered the bones of them that were hanged.
21.14: And the bones of Saul and of Jonathan his sonne buried they in the coutrey of Beniamin in Zelah, in the grave of Kish his father: and when they had perfourmed all that the King had commanded, God was then appeased with the land.
21.15: Again the Philistims had war with Israel: and David went down, and his servants with him, and they fought against the Philistims, and David fainted.
21.16: Then Ishi-benob which was of the sonnes of Haraphah (the head of whose spear wayed three hundreth shekels of brass) even he being girded with a new sword, thought to have slain David.
21.17: But Abishai the sonne of Zeruiah succoured him, and smote the Philistim, and killed him. Then Dauids men sware unto him, saying, Thou shalt goe no more out with us to battell, lest thou quench the light of Israel.
21.18: And after this also there was a battell with the Philistims at Gob, then Sibbechai the Hushathite slew Saph, which was one of ye sonnes of Haraphah.
21.19: And there was yet another battel in Gob with the Philistims, where Elhanah the sonne of Iaare-oregim, a Bethlehemite slew Goliath the Gittite: the staff of whose spear was like a weauers beam.
21.20: Afterward there was also a battel in Gath, where was a man of a great stature, and had on euerie hand six fingers, and on euerie foot six toes, four and twentie in nomber: who was also the sonne of Haraphah.
21.21: And when hee reviled Israel, Jonathan the sonne of Shima the brother of David slew him.
21.22: These four were borne to Haraphah in Gath, and died by the hand of David and by the hands of his servants.

22.1: And David spake the woordes of this song unto the Lord, what time the Lord had delivered him out of the handes of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul.
22.2: And he sayd, The Lord is my rock and my fortress, and he that delivereth mee.
22.3: God is my strength, in him will I trust: my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my hie tower and my refuge: my Sauiour, thou hast saved me from violence.
22.4: I will call on the Lord, who is worthy to be praysed: so shall I be safe from mine enemies.
22.5: For the pangs of death have compassed me: the floods of vngodlinesse have made mee afrayd.
22.6: The sorowes of the grave compassed mee about: the snares of death overtook mee.
22.7: But in my tribulation did I call upon the Lord, and crie to my God, and he did hear my voyce out of his temple, and my crie did enter into his eares.
22.8: Then the earth trembled and quaked: the foundations of the heavens mooued and shook, because he was angrie.
22.9: Smoke went out at his nostrels, and consuming fire out of his mouth: coles were kindled thereat.
22.10: He bowed the heavens also, and came down, and darkenes was under his feet.
22.11: And he rode upon Cherub and did flie, and hee was seen upon the winges of the wind.
22.12: And hee made darkenesse a Tabernacle round about him, even the gatherings of waters, and the cloudes of the ayre.
22.13: At the brightness of his presence the coles of fire were kindled.
22.14: The Lord thundred from heaven, and the most hie gave his voyce.
22.15: He shot arrowes also, and scattered them: to wit, lightning, and destroyed them.
22.16: The chanels also of the sea appeared, even the foundations of the world were discovered by the rebuking of the Lord, and at the blast of the breath of his nostrels.
22.17: He sent from above, and took me: hee drew me out of many waters.
22.18: He delivered me from my strong enemie, and from them that hated me: for they were too strong for me.
22.19: They prevented me in the day of my calamitie, but the Lord was my stay,
22.20: And brought me foorth into a large place: he delivered me, because he fauoured me.
22.21: The Lord rewarded me according to my righteousness: according to the pureness of mine handes he recompensed me.
22.22: For I kept the wayes of the Lord, and did not wickedly against my God.
22.23: For all his lawes were before me, and his statutes: I did not depart therefrom.
22.24: I was upright also toward him, and have kept me from my wickedness.
22.25: Therefore the Lord did reward me according to my righteousness, according to my pureness before his eyes.
22.26: With the godly thou wilt shew thy self godly: with the upright man thou wilt shew thy self upright.
22.27: With the pure thou wilt shew thy self pure, and with the froward thou wilt shew thy self froward.
22.28: Thus thou wilt save the poor people: but thine eyes are upon the hautie to humble them.
22.29: Surely thou art my light, O Lord: and the Lord will lighten my darkenes.
22.30: For by thee have I broken through an host, and by my God have I leaped over a wall.
22.31: The way of God is vncorrupt: the word of the Lord is tryed in the fire: he is a shield to all that trust in him.
22.32: For who is God besides the Lord? and who is mightie, save our God?
22.33: God is my strength in battel, and maketh my way upright.
22.34: He maketh my feet like hindes feet, and hath set me upon mine hie places.
22.35: He teacheth mine handes to fight, so that a bow of brass is broken with mine armes.
22.36: Thou hast also given me the shield of thy salvation, and thy loving kindness hath caused me to increase.
22.37: Thou hast inlarged my steppes under me, and mine heeles have not slid.
22.38: I have pursued mine enemies and destroyed them, and have not turned again until I had consumed them.
22.39: Yea, I have consumed them and thrust them through, and they shall not arise, but shall fall under my feet.
22.40: For thou hast girded me with power to battell, and them that arose against me, hast thou subdued under me.
22.41: And thou hast given me the neckes of mine enemies, that I might destroy them that hate me.
22.42: They looked about, but there was none to save them, even unto the Lord, but he answered them not.
22.43: Then did I beat them as small as the dust of the earth: I did tread them flat as the clay of the street, and did spread them abroad.
22.44: Thou hast also delivered me from the contentions of my people: thou hast preserved me to be the head over nations: the people which I knew not, doe serve me.
22.45: Strangers shalbe in subiection to me: assoone as they hear, they shall obey me.
22.46: Strangers shall shrinke away, and fear in their priuie chambers.
22.47: Let the Lord live, and blessed be my strength: and God, even the force of my salvation be exalted.
22.48: It is God that giveth me power to revenge me, and subdue the people under me,
22.49: And rescueth me from mine enemies: (thou also hast lift me up from them that rose against me, thou hast delivered me from the cruel man.
22.50: Therefore I will praise thee, O Lord amog the nations, and will sing unto thy Name)
22.51: He is the tower of salvation for his King, and sheweth mercie to his anointed, even to David, and to his seed for ever.

23.1: These also be the last wordes of David, David the sonne of Ishai saith, even the man who was set up on hie, the Anointed of the God of Jacob, and the sweet singer of Israel saith,
23.2: The Spirit of the Lord spake by me, and his word was in my tongue.
23.3: The God of Israel spake to me, ye strength of Israel said, Thou shalt bear rule over men, being just, and ruling in the fear of God.
23.4: Even as the morning light when the sunne riseth, the morning, I say, without cloudes, so shall mine house be, and not as the grass of the earth is by the bright rain.
23.5: For so shall not mine house be with God: for he hath made with me an everlasting covenant, perfite in all pointes, and sure: therefore all mine health and whole desire is, that he will not make it grow so.
23.6: But the wicked shalbe every one as thornes thrust away, because they can not be taken with handes.
23.7: But the man that shall touch them, must be defensed with yron, or with the shaft of a spear: and they shall be burnt with fire in the same place.
23.8: These be the names of the mightie men whom David had. He that sat in the seat of wisedome, being chief of the princes, was Adino of Ezni, he slew eight hundreth at one time.
23.9: And after him was Eleazar the sonne of Dodo, the sonne of Ahohi, one of the three worthies with David, when they defied the Philistims gathered there to battel, when the men of Israel were gone up.
23.10: He arose and smote the Philistims until his hand was wearie, and his hand clave unto the sword: and the Lord gave great victorie the same day, and the people returned after him onely to spoyle.
23.11: After him was Shammah the sonne of Age the Hararite: for the Philistims assembled at a town, where was a piece of a field full of lentils, and the people fled from the Philistims.
23.12: But he stood in the middes of the field, and defended it, and slew the Philistims: so the Lord gave great victorie.
23.13: Afterward three of the thirtie captaines went down, and came to David in the harvest time unto the cave of Adullam, and the host of the Philistims pitched in the valley of Rephaim.
23.14: And David was then in an hold, and the garison of ye Philistims was then in Beth-lehem.
23.15: And David longed, and said, Oh, that one would give me to drink of the water of the well of Beth-lehem, which is by the gate.
23.16: The the three mightie brake into the host of the Philistims, and drew water out of the well of Beth-lehem that was by the gate, and took and brought it to David, who would not drink thereof, but powred it for an offring unto ye Lord,
23.17: And said, O Lord, be it far from me, that I should doe this. Is not this the blood of the men that went in ieopardie of their lives? therefore he would not drink it. These things did these three mightie men.
23.18: And Abishai the brother of Joab, the sonne of Zeruiah, was chief among the three, and he lifted up his spear against three hundreth, and slew them, and he had the name among the three.
23.19: For he was most excellent of the three, and was their captain, but he attained not unto the first three.
23.20: And Benaiah the sonne of Jehoiada the sonne of a valiant man, which had done many actes, and was of Kabzeel, slew two strong men of Moab: he went down also, and slew a lyon in the middes of a pit in the time of snow.
23.21: And he slew an Egyptian a man of great stature, and the Egyptian had a spear in his hand: but he went down to him with a staff, and plucked the spear out of the Egyptians hand, and slew him with his own spear.
23.22: These things did Benaiah the sonne of Jehoiada, and had the name among the three worthies.
23.23: He was honourable among thirtie, but he atteined not to the first three: and David made him of his counsel.
23.24: Asahel the brother of Joab was one of the thirtie: Elhanan the sonne of Dodo of Beth-lehem:
23.25: Shammah the Harodite: Elika ye Harodite:
23.26: Helez the Paltite: Ira the sonne of Ikkesh the Tekoite:
23.27: Abiezer the Anethothite: Mebunnai the Husathite:
23.28: Zalmon an Ahohite: Maharai the Netophathite:
23.29: Heleb the sonne of Baanah a Netophathite: Ittai the sonne of Ribai of Gibeah of the children of Beniamin:
23.30: Benaiah the Pirathonite: Hiddai of the river of Gaash:
23.31: Abi-albon the Arbathite: Azmaveth the Barhumite:
23.32: Elihaba the Shaalbonite: of the sonnes of Jashen, Jonathan:
23.33: Shammah the Hararite: Ahiam the sonne of Sharar the Hamrite:
23.34: Eliphelet the sonne of Ahasbai the sonne of Maachathi: Eliam the sonne of Ahithophel the Gilonite:
23.35: Hezrai the Carmelite: Paarai the Arbite:
23.36: Igal the sonne of Nathan of Zobah: Bani the Gadite:
23.37: Zelek the Ammonite: Naharai the Becrothite, the armour bearer of Joab the sonne of Zeruiah:
23.38: Ira the Ithrite: Gareb the Ithrite:
23.39: Uriiah the Hittite, thirtie and seven in all.

24.1: And the wrath of the Lord was again kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them, in that he said, Goe, number Israel and Judah.
24.2: For the King said to Joab the captain of the host, which was with him, Goe speedily now through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan even to Beer-sheba, and nomber ye the people, that I may know the nomber of the people.
24.3: And Joab said unto the King, The Lord thy God increase the people an hundreth fold more then they be, and that the eyes of my lord the King may see it: but why doeth my lord the King desire this thing?
24.4: Notwithstanding the Kings word prevailed against Joab and against the captaines of the host: therefore Joab and the captaines of the host went out from the presence of the King to nomber the people of Israel.
24.5: And they passed over Iorden, and pitched in Aroer at the right side of the citie that is in the middes of the valley of Gad and toward Jazer.
24.6: Then they came to Gilead, and to Tahtim-hodshi, so they came to Dan Iaan, and so about to Zidon,
24.7: And came to the fortress of Tyrus and to all the cities of the Hivites and of the Canaanites, and went toward the South of Judah, even to Beer-sheba.
24.8: So when they had gone about all the land, they returned to Jerusalem at the end of nine moneths and twentie dayes.
24.9: And Joab delivered the nomber and summe of the people unto the King: and there were in Israel eight hundreth thousand strong men that drew swordes, and the men of Judah were five hundreth thousand men.
24.10: Then Dauids heart smote him, after that he had numbred the people: and David said unto the Lord, I have sinned exceedingly in that I have done: therefore now, Lord, I beseech thee, take away the trespass of thy servant: for I have done very foolishly.
24.11: And when David was up in the morning, the word of the Lord came unto the Prophet Gad Dauids Seer, saying,
24.12: Go, and say unto David, Thus saith ye Lord, I offer thee three thinges, chuse thee which of them I shall doe unto thee.
24.13: So Gad came to David, and shewed him, and said unto him, Wilt thou that seven yeeres famine come upon thee in thy land, or wilt thou flee three moneths before thine enemies, they following thee, or that there bee three dayes pestilence in thy land? now advise thee, and see, what answer I shall give to him that sent me.
24.14: And David said unto Gad, I am in a wonderful strait: let us fall now into the hand of the Lord, (for his mercies are great) and let mee not fall into the hand of man.
24.15: So the Lord sent a pestilece in Israel, from the morning even to the time appointed: and there dyed of the people from Dan even to Beer-sheba seuentie thousand men.
24.16: And when the Angel stretched out his hand upon Jerusalem to destroy it, the Lord repented of the evil, and said to the Angel that destroyed the people, It is sufficient, hold now thine hand. And the Angel of the Lord was by the threshing place of Araunah the Jebusite.
24.17: And David spake unto the Lord (when he saw the Angel that smote the people) and said, Behold, I have sinned, yea, I have done wickedly: but these sheep, what have they done? let thine hand, I pray thee, be against mee and against my fathers house.
24.18: So Gad came the same day to David, and said unto him, Go up, rear an altar unto the Lord in the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
24.19: And David (according to the saying of Gad) went up, as the Lord had commanded.
24.20: And Araunah looked, and saw the King and his servants coming toward him, and Araunah went out, and bowed himself before the King on his face to the ground,
24.21: And Araunah said, Wherefore is my lord the King come to his servant? Then David answered, To bye the threshing floor of thee for to build an altar unto the Lord, that the plague may cease from the people.
24.22: Then Araunah said unto David, Let my lord the King take and offer what seemeth him good in his eyes: behold the oxen for the burnt offring, and charets, and the instruments of the oxen for wood.
24.23: (All these things did Araunah as a King give unto the King: and Araunah said unto the King, The Lord thy God be fauourable unto thee)
24.24: Then the King said unto Araunah, Not so, but I will bye it of thee at a price, and will not offer burnt offring unto ye Lord my God of that which doeth cost me nothing. So David bought the threshing floor, and the oxen for fiftie shekels of silver.
24.25: And David built there an altar unto the Lord, and offred burnt offrings and peace offrings, and the Lord was appeased toward ye land, and the plague ceased from Israel.
